name: Elena Torres
headline: Fifteen years of restaurant P&Ls — first from inside the kitchen, then across the ledger.
paragraphs: Elena ran the numbers for her family's two taquerias through the years when a bad month meant deciding which vendor got paid first. The bookkeeper they could afford touched the books quarterly; every problem was three months old before anyone saw it.

She retrained as an accountant with one intention: build the service her family never had. Torres Books & Margins is that service — weekly closes, invoice-level reconciliation, and a monthly conversation in the language of plate cost and labor mix, not debits and credits.
The practice stays small on purpose. Every client works directly with Elena, and the roster is capped at the number of restaurants one person can genuinely know week to week.
signoff: See you on the Tuesday call,
